module_title: Important Articles: Union & States - Basic Understanding
introduction: The Indian Constitution elegantly mirrors the structure of the Central (Union) government at the State level. Part V (Articles 52-151) deals with the Union, while Part VI (Articles 152-237) deals with the States. Mastering the foundational articles of the Executive and Legislature is crucial for beginners.

core_concepts.title: The Executive Heads (Art 52 & 153)
core_concepts.description: Article 52 states 'There shall be a President of India'. Article 153 mirrors this at the state level: 'There shall be a Governor for each State'.

core_concepts.title: The Real Heads (Art 75 & 164)
core_concepts.description: Article 75 deals with the appointment of the Prime Minister and Union Ministers by the President. Article 164 deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister and State Ministers by the Governor.

core_concepts.title: The Legislatures (Art 79 & 168)
core_concepts.description: Article 79 constitutes the Parliament (President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha). Article 168 constitutes the State Legislature (Governor + Legislative Assembly + Legislative Council, where applicable).

core_concepts.title: The Top Courts (Art 124 & 214)
core_concepts.description: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court of India. Article 214 establishes High Courts for the States.

important_entities.name: The +89 Rule
important_entities.significance: For many core articles, adding 89 to the Union Article gives you the corresponding State Article (e.g., 74 + 89 = 163; 75 + 89 = 164).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse these two. Remember: Art 74 is about the existence of the Council of Ministers to 'aid and advise' the President. Art 75 is about their 'appointment and tenure'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.trick_title: Supreme Court vs. High Court Articles
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Supreme Court is Article 124. Swap the first two digits (214), and you get the Article for High Courts.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the starting articles of the major branches: Executive (52), Parliament (79), Supreme Court (124), CAG (148).
Identify direct parallel articles using the +89 trick to cut your memorization effort in half.
